html:
The Fireburn was a revolt of plantation workers on St Croix in October 1878, in which much of the town of Frederiksted and many estates were burned. It was the largest labour revolt in Danish colonial history.

Thirty years after emancipation, workers were bound to yearly contracts with low pay, could change employers only on one day a year and could not leave the island freely. A rumour that a worker had died in police custody set off the rising.

Danish troops put it down; dozens of workers were killed and some executed. Three women, called Queen Mary, Queen Agnes and Queen Mathilda, were tried as leaders; a statue of Queen Mary and her fellow rebels was raised in Copenhagen in 2018, the first public monument there to a Black woman, as Denmark faced its slave trade past.
